pred_ddx.label: Chronic Angle Closure Glaucoma with Anterior Displacement of the Lens

Chronic Angle Closure Glaucoma with Ante: The patient's symptoms of acute pain and reduced vision, combined with the examination findings of high intraocular pressure, flat anterior chambers, and signs of acute angle closure, suggest a diagnosis of chronic angle closure glaucoma. The ultrasound biomicroscopy (UBM) findings of an anteriorly displaced crystalline lens with extensive irido-lenticular contact and peripheral anterior synechiae (PAS) closing the angles completely in both eyes support this diagnosis.
Lens-Induced Angle Closure Glaucoma: The patient's history of treatment with oral acetazolamide and 4% pilocarpine drops, and the examination findings of a mid-peripheral patent laser iridotomy, suggest that the angle closure may be related to the lens. The UBM findings of an anteriorly displaced crystalline lens with extensive irido-lenticular contact and PAS support this diagnosis, and the patient's symptoms and examination findings are consistent with lens-induced angle closure glaucoma.
